plan: To preserve capital, sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, METU, MSFU, MUU, PLTU) to zero.
Trim QQQI to 20% to meet the single name concentration mandate.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation and reduces overall portfolio risk.
It aims for a steady, low-drawdown approach with a focus on quality and broad index exposure.
conservative.read: This conservative plan targets a realistic ~1.5%/month return, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and lowering concentration, but still carries market exposure.

plan: For balanced growth, trim leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, MSFU, SPAL, MUU, PLTU) to small positions.
Trim QQQI to 25% to meet the single name concentration mandate.
This plan blends broad index and quality tech with reduced leverage.
It aims for risk-first growth while maintaining a cash buffer.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets a realistic ~2.5%/month return, aiming for risk-first growth. It reduces leverage and concentration, offering a moderate risk profile with potential for market participation.

plan: For aggressive growth, trim QQQI to 25% to meet the single name concentration mandate.
Add new positions in high-scoring scanner setups like AVGO, AMZN, TXN, and AMZU.
This plan leans into leverage and concentrates in strong long setups.
It aims to stretch growth, accepting higher risk for potentially greater returns.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets a realistic ~4%/month return, but comes with significantly higher risk. Expect larger drawdowns and be aware of leveraged ETF decay; strict stop discipline is crucial.

plan: To prioritize income, sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, METU, MSFU, MUU, PLTU) to zero.
Add to QQQI, increasing its allocation to 30% for enhanced income exposure.
This plan rotates into income-focused ETFs and broad index for steady distributions.
It aims for low drawdown and reliable income over growth, with a cash buffer.
income.read: This income plan targets a realistic ~1%/month return, prioritizing steady monthly distributions. While aiming for low drawdown, distributions are variable, and NAV can still fall in market selloffs.
